subject: physics
title: Newton's second law and inertia
key_idea: The resultant force on an object equals its mass times its acceleration, F = m × a. Acceleration is proportional to force and inversely proportional to mass. Inertial mass measures how hard it is to change an object's velocity.

blocks.text: Newton's second law links the resultant force on an object, its mass and its acceleration. A bigger force gives a bigger acceleration. A bigger mass gives a smaller one.

items: The acceleration is **proportional** to the resultant force: double the force, double the acceleration.
The acceleration is **inversely proportional** to the mass: double the mass, halve the acceleration.

An object slowing down has a resultant force against its velocity.
If the answer asks for significant figures, round only at the end.

blocks.text: Some objects are harder to speed up or slow down than others. This is the idea of inertia.

items.meaning: The tendency of objects to continue in their state of rest or of uniform motion.
A measure of how difficult it is to change the velocity of an object. It is the ratio of force over acceleration.

blocks.label: Inertial mass
where: m: inertial mass in kilograms, kg
a: acceleration in metres per second squared, m/s²

items: A large inertial mass needs a large force for the same acceleration.
A small inertial mass changes velocity easily.
A lighter child needs less force to be slowed in a crash, so a narrower seatbelt can be used.
(Higher tier) Inertia is the tendency to keep the same velocity.
(Higher tier) Bigger inertial mass means a bigger force for the same acceleration.

checks.q: A 1200 kg car accelerates at 2.5 m/s². Calculate the resultant force.
A resultant force of 2.0 N acts on a 0.50 kg trolley. Calculate its acceleration.
(Higher tier) Explain why a lorry needs a bigger force than a car to get the same acceleration.
checks.a: The lorry has a bigger (inertial) mass, so by F = m × a it needs a bigger force.

exam_phrases: Give your answer to 2 significant figures

mistakes.right: Rearrange first. Mass = force ÷ acceleration, so m = 1800 ÷ 25 = 72 kg.

mistakes.wrong: The acceleration is 0.625 m/s², so I have finished.
mistakes.right: Round to the significant figures asked for: 0.63 m/s². The rounding is a separate mark.

mistakes.wrong: The resultant force on a decelerating person must be given as a positive number only.
mistakes.right: A negative force is allowed for a deceleration. F = 75 × 60 = 4500 N, and −4500 N is accepted.

worked_example.question:
A student investigated the acceleration of a trolley.

The resultant force on the trolley was 0.375 N.
The mass of the trolley was 0.60 kg.

Calculate the acceleration of the trolley.
Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
answer_points: Substitute into F = m a: 0.375 = 0.60 × a
Round to 2 significant figures: a = 0.63 m/s²
worked_example.tip: One mark for each line. The last mark is for the rounding to 2 significant figures.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Inertial mass is a measure of how difficult it is to change the velocity of an object. It is defined as the ratio of force over acceleration.
Recognise and use the symbol ∝ for proportional, and ~ for an approximate value.

mistakes.right: Do not allow Ns. The unit of force is N or newtons.
A power of ten wrong scores 1 mark at most. 0.10 × 2.0 = 0.20 N.
Inertial mass is force over acceleration: 450 / 0.35 = 1300 kg.

mistakes.right: Divide, do not multiply: mass = 4000 ÷ 5 = 800 kg.

mistakes.wrong: A lighter car needs less force for the same acceleration.
mistakes.right: Start with F = ma. With the same engine force, a smaller mass gives a greater acceleration.
The answer is 800 kg. Writing 0.8 scores only two of the three marks.

worked_example.question:
A roller coaster car moves down a slope with an acceleration of 5 m/s².

The force on the roller coaster car is 4000 N.

Calculate the mass of the roller coaster car.
worked_example.tip: Check the answer first: 800 kg scores all 3 marks. Giving 0.8 instead of 800 scores 2 marks.

blocks.text: To estimate a force, pick a sensible mass and multiply it by the acceleration.

items: A family car has a mass of about 1500 kg.
At a deceleration of 6 m/s², F = 1500 × 6 = 9000 N.
Any car mass from 400 to 3500 kg is allowed.
